acceptance: Supported-interface inventory maps every previously generated product contract to an owning explicit reference destination and proving content check; no empty page or missing-interface success.

Generated reference pages retain useful signatures, parameter/default distinctions, behavior, errors and examples; deliberate removal of filler/false claims is recorded and public facade forwarding remains intact.

The interrogate configuration, both hardcoded gate consumers, the Make public target/help behavior and the docs workflow badge are retired atomically in their own PR, before any public docstring deletion lands and with no percentage replacement; API reference content and contract tests carry the requirement instead.
Current Make inventory regenerates through the supported entrypoint; historical monolith baseline/migration evidence is byte-preserved and any current receipt diff is explained.
Search establishes no remaining obsolete interrogate/docstring-presence consumer. Documentation rendering and contract gates pass without weakening other CI thresholds.

Public reference page ownership is handed to module tasks by exact path; shared indexes/navigation remain singleton-owned. The 79 autodoc directives on 27 pages are retargeted to maintained reference content or removed before the docstrings they render are deleted.

Every cross-module docstring or source-text reader has migrated or has a verified consumer-before-producer dependency; local consumers are explicitly owned. Verify whether display_benchmark_list (no production caller) needs any change before treating it as a prerequisite. A release note covers the loss of help(), Click help and MCP tool descriptions.

description:
Singleton owner of docs/conf.py, shared API/reference infrastructure, supported-interface reference migration, pyproject interrogate configuration, Make docstring target/help, docs.yml coverage job/badge, current Make inventory and dedicated contract-check tests. This prerequisite owns these files before later shared-infrastructure cleanup; no overlapping writers. Target: zero discretionary explanatory comments and authored explanatory docstrings in maintained first-party code. Only proven minimum machine directives and unavoidable provenance-bound required notices remain. Useful product strings must have an actual consumer; no inert constants, unused strings, fake metadata or dynamic __doc__ replacements. Never broaden lint/type/coverage ignores, weaken assertions, or turn unknown ownership/parser coverage into an exclusion.

Map supported public APIs and consequential internal boundaries to reviewed external reference pages before removing their source docstrings. Keep source-derived signatures where useful. Replace/retarget content-producing autodoc directives; verify behavior/errors/examples and per-interface contracts, not merely successful rendering. Correct incomplete parameters and unsupported assurance; discard filler rather than exporting every sentence. Preserve public wrappers and compatibility unless separately approved.

Atomically replace all hardcoded 90% interrogate consumers in pyproject, Make and docs.yml, including orphan badge generation. Remove obsolete tool consumers only after search. Use a useful content/reference/contract gate, not another prose percentage or NLP scorer. Regenerate current make/inventory.json through its supported helper, preserving monolith-baseline.json and historical migration proofs. This task prepares shared infrastructure; module tasks subsequently own only assigned module reference pages. Execution guard: creation of this TODO is planning, not approval to execute the reviewed cleanup. Obtain later implementation authorization. Use a separate linked worktree and agent-write-preflight; preserve unrelated work. Freeze nonoverlapping code/test/doc paths with the integrator before dispatch. Ordinary independent PRs target develop; serialize shared test-lock checks and integration, not module edits. Required native/external soundness review remains mandatory, with no auto-merge bypass. No live cloud/stress, deployment, publication, historical-result rewriting, or unapproved external-repository writes.
Known shared internal rationale also migrates before parallel deletion: single-flight/concurrency ADR and proof matrix, driver drain-before-commit contract, TPC reference-seed/timing/framing guides, MCP redaction threat model, slim-corpus independence/calibration ADRs, quality exception policy and workaround index. Preserve active symbol/section navigation and frozen historical citations. Assign later module-local pages exclusively; newly discovered shared content blocks the affected deletion until its owning integrator publishes the destination.
This prerequisite also owns the narrow cross-module runtime bridge in benchbox/core/results/display.py:display_benchmark_list and its dedicated display tests: replace benchmark-class __doc__ reads with the existing canonical registry descriptions BEFORE any benchmark module can delete class docstrings. It does not sweep the rest of results/display.py. Inventory any other cross-module source/docstring reader and migrate it here or add an explicit consumer-before-producer dependency before dispatch. Local Click/FastMCP/argparse migrations remain within their owning module before local deletion.
